title: Lesson 45 - Creating Segments: Types, Filters, Calculated Insights, and Engagement Data as Criteria
description: Manage segments within Data 360, covering segment types, filters and criteria, and using calculated insights and engagement data as criteria.

questions.question: A consultant needs a segment whose criteria reference a customer lifetime value score computed across several sources. What should be used?
options: A data lake object attribute copied into the segment
A calculated insight added as a segment criterion
questions.explanation: Calculated insights are metrics computed across data and can be added to extend a segment, which is exactly how criteria reference a computed value rather than a raw attribute.

questions.question: Which statement about the lookback window is correct?
options: It has no effect once the segment is saved
Container criteria can specify a narrower window that takes precedence over the segment level setting
It defaults to 30 days and cannot be changed
It applies only to dynamic segments
questions.explanation: Container criteria take precedence over the segment level window; the default is 90 days and can extend to your organization maximum, and it applies to standard segments generally.

questions.question: A segment built on a data model object with a composite key returns inaccurate counts. What does the documentation recommend?
options: Use data model objects with a single, unique primary key for segmentation
questions.explanation: The segment canvas relies on single field relationships and cannot join on all fields of a composite key, so the recommendation is to use a data model object with a single unique primary key.
